title: Add graceful shutdown with signal handling
description: Implements process signal listeners (SIGINT, SIGTERM) to stop accepting new connections and wait for in‑flight requests to finish before exiting. This prevents dropped requests during deployments and improves reliability in production environments.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while a long‑running request is in progress and verify the server stops accepting new connections but completes the pending request before process exit
Send SIGINT to a running server with no active requests and verify it closes immediately and exits with code 0
acceptance: The server must correctly handle SIGINT and SIGTERM, stop accepting new connections, wait up to a configurable timeout (default 30 s) for active requests to finish, then exit with status 0. If the timeout expires, the process should force‑exit with status 1. All existing test suites must still pass.
reason: Deployments and container orchestration platforms rely on graceful shutdown to avoid 5xx errors. Adding this feature eliminates a common production pain point without adding external dependencies, aligning with yantraverse's zero‑dependency philosophy.
